title: Truthfulness of Scripture
definition: The truthfulness of Scripture is the doctrine that God's Word is completely trustworthy, reliable, and true in all that it affirms.
summary: Because God is truthful and cannot lie, His Word is trustworthy and dependable.
christFocus: Jesus consistently treated Scripture as true, authoritative, and trustworthy, affirming its reliability throughout His ministry.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
The Bible is not merely a collection of religious opinions or human reflections about God. Scripture is God's revelation, and because God is perfectly truthful, His Word can be trusted completely. Throughout history, believers have relied upon Scripture as a dependable foundation for doctrine, discipleship, worship, and daily living.

The truthfulness of Scripture does not require believers to understand every difficult passage immediately. Rather, it means that God's Word faithfully communicates what He intends to reveal. Christians approach Scripture with confidence because its ultimate author is God Himself.

This doctrine provides stability in a world filled with competing claims, changing opinions, and uncertainty.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: Many voices claim authority today, often contradicting one another. Understanding the truthfulness of Scripture gives believers a reliable foundation upon which to build their faith, convictions, and decisions.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: When cultural opinions, personal feelings, or popular teachings conflict with Scripture, choose to trust God's Word. Build your worldview upon biblical truth rather than shifting human ideas.
